mechanism: Core capital goods orders (nondefense capital goods excluding aircraft) measure business demand for equipment and forward capital-spending plans. Rising orders growth signals firmer investment and earnings ahead (risk-on); slowing orders are an early sign of softening demand.
key_finding: As known at the time (real-time NEWORDER vintages), the rule selected on in-sample data uses yoy / T_roll_p25 at L11 (IS Sharpe 0.76); held-out OOS Sharpe 0.89 versus buy-and-hold SPY 1.00.
caveats: The strategy is search-selected and needs a frozen-rule holdout confirmation.
Core capital goods orders are nominal and revised after the advance report, so the as-known-at-the-time and revised tracks differ through revisions as well as release timing.
The 2020-21 collapse and rebound in orders is an extreme outlier inside the test window.
The test window was seen by the previously published runs, so it is not a frozen hold-out.
narrative_summary: Core capital goods orders (NEWORDER) growth is tested as a procyclical capital-spending overlay for SPY. The data is NEWORDER, not total manufacturing new orders (AMTMNO).

data_provenance.source: FRED / ALFRED (U.S. Census Bureau, advance durable goods / M3)
